author: @marc.kaz
title_or_hook: The video-to-clips stack: WhisperX + PySceneDetect + Auto-Editor + Remotion + FFmpeg (all five repos named in the caption)
summary: A complete, composable pipeline for turning long videos into short clips, in data-flow order, with every repo URL printed in the post's own caption. WhisperX (m-bain/whisperX) transcribes speech with word-level timestamps and speaker diarization (Whisper plus wav2vec2 forced alignment); PySceneDetect (Breakthrough/PySceneDetect) detects scene cuts and transitions (Python plus OpenCV) so clips break at real boundaries; Auto-Editor (WyattBlue/auto-editor) cuts silence and dead air by audio-volume analysis; Remotion (remotion-dev/remotion) renders the final clips programmatically, video as React components, so captions, overlays, telestration and branding are code and batch-renderable; FFmpeg is the encode and package layer underneath. The poster is a curator; the components are the origins. Plugs into the GSE Content OS directly: it is the automation layer for the standing format (real footage, short transformative clips, telestrated, commentary-led, never AI slideshow substitutes), extending the self-hosted Reclip downloader (Reclip fetches; this stack cuts and finishes). Remotion compositions can be driven by the engine's own verdict JSON so a clip renders from the pick object with no manual step. Risks: Remotion is not MIT, it uses its own license (free for individuals and small teams, paid company license at larger scale), verify terms before building a rendering service on it; the other four are permissive open source (WhisperX BSD-2-Clause, PySceneDetect BSD-3-Clause, Auto-Editor Unlicense, FFmpeg LGPL/GPL depending on build). WhisperX wants a GPU for speed. First test: one already-owned long recording through WhisperX plus PySceneDetect, then one Remotion-rendered 15-second captioned clip; if the render step is slower to template than the current hand process, keep WhisperX and PySceneDetect and drop the renderer.
engine_training_value: Real and direct: WhisperX output is labelled speech data, word-level timestamps plus speaker labels for coach and QB press conferences and interviews, exactly the interviews and coach-speak lane of testable signals; transcripts live wherever the source audio lives and the labels are generated by the tool itself. PySceneDetect cut lists are weaker labels (event-boundary candidates for broadcast footage). No betting-market labels; the value is the situational and context corpus.
provenance: m-bain/whisperX, Breakthrough/PySceneDetect, WyattBlue/auto-editor, remotion-dev/remotion, FFmpeg/FFmpeg (poster @marc.kaz is curator)

author: @githubsignals
title_or_hook: Calibrain Harness: a forward-testing harness that scores a trading model honestly (VERIFIED at repo level; its own published results are negative)
summary: An open-source forward-testing harness for fast classification models on crypto perpetuals, built around one discipline: every model answer is a forecast that will be checked. On each closed bar it asks the model (Kairos via Minara Cloud, or Jev via TypeSafe, both behind one POST /v1/systemone interface) a fixed set of 7 labellable questions, shows the model the instrument's own historical base rates for each question, blends the model's probabilities with those base rates through a calibration layer whose weight is fitted on labelled outcomes, converts to expected value in code, and trades only what clears the gates, on Bybit testnet only, hard-coded, no mainnet switch. Every prediction is scored, traded or not: Brier and RPS skill vs climatology and vs the base rates shown, AUC, reliability diagrams, PIT, walk-forward validation with 90% intervals. Its own README publishes the early results honestly: 10.5 hours, 769 decisions, 40 trades, net -2,601.01 USDT on testnet; strict mode took zero trades in 3h45m because base rates alone are never positive-EV after costs. Repo facts verified this run: MIT, about 295 stars, 60 forks, 218 commits, created 2026-11-10 (four days old), Python 3.12 plus Next.js 16 terminal UI, no releases yet. Plugs into the GSE prediction engine's evaluation and calibration layer as a design specimen, not as trading code: labellable questions, base rates shown to the model, fitted calibration blend weights, strict-mode pass discipline, and every decision scored traded-or-not mirror the engine's own doctrines. First test is a read, not a run: calibration.py, policy.py, and the VALID screen metrics against the engine's current calibration implementation. Running it live needs a Kairos or Jev key plus Bybit testnet keys; none were created.
metrics_or_datasets: Brier and RPS skill vs climatology and base rates
engine_training_value: The strongest in the run, as method: the repo is a worked example of turning model outputs into labelled outcomes with base rates attached; its SQLite store (every request, answer, label, trade, run) is the exact record shape a training and eval loop needs, and its v1 to v2 lesson (show base rates or the model hallucinates movement) is a measured result about a training input rather than an opinion. No sports data; the dataset it generates is crypto bars, useless to GSE as data, valuable as a template for GSE's own decision-store schema.

author: @ariacodez
title_or_hook: Audio8-TTS-Realistic: free voice cloning from a few seconds of audio (VERIFIED model; the danger framing is the poster's, the capability is real)
summary: Audio8-TTS-Realistic-0.6b (Edge0 / Edge0-AI, released late Oct 2026): a 0.6-billion-parameter open-weight text-to-speech model with zero-shot voice cloning. Give it one short, clean reference clip plus the exact transcript of that clip, and it speaks new text in that voice, at 44.1 kHz, in 23 languages, running locally on a consumer GPU (about 1.2 GB weights). Architecture per the model coverage: a DualAR speech LM in the Fish Audio S2 Pro lineage (24-layer slow transformer predicting semantic tokens, 4-layer fast transformer predicting codec codebooks, neural RVQ codec). A LiteRT conversion (litert-community) runs it on-device, and an OVOS plugin exists. Verified this run via the model's Hugging Face lineage and multiple independent write-ups. Free, Apache-2.0, open weights; a free Hugging Face playground (ZeroGPU) exists and was not opened, and nothing was cloned. Plugs into the GSE Content OS, in the Nova lane specifically, with the consent line drawn hard: a local free TTS that holds a consistent character voice replaces paid per-character spend for drafts, scratch tracks, and internal review cuts; it is a candidate for final voice only if it passes Garrett's naturalness bar on a real Nova line, which is his call. Consent is the whole risk surface: cloning a real person's voice without permission is impersonation regardless of the license. First test: clone Garrett's own voice (or Nova's established production voice, with his approval) from a clean 10-second clip and A/B one known test line blind against the current voice on naturalness only.
engine_training_value: none - context only for the prediction engine. (For the Content OS it is generation infrastructure, not training data; its existence is, however, a labelled fact for Family Shield's threat model: a convincing clone needs only about 3 to 10 seconds of clean audio.)

author: @ianjenkins_hitting
title_or_hook: Bat weight beats bat length: a barrel-control argument, full script in the caption
summary: A hitting-instruction argument with an actual mechanism: hitters shop by bat length, but the controlling variable is barrel control, and a slightly heavier or more end-loaded bat can improve control because the hitter can feel where the barrel is (proprioception), whereas a too-light bat is unfeelable and therefore uncontrollable. Prescriptions: if a light bat already gives you barrel control, keep it; if you can't find the barrel, experiment upward in weight; if a heavier bat still doesn't fix control, choke up (shortens effective length without a new bat). Closes with an explicit anti-dogma line ("Nothing I say is law"). The caption carries the complete spoken script, so this is the rare reel whose full payload is text-recoverable. It is a technique post, not a product; no bat is sold in the recovered text. A single coach's heuristic, UNVERIFIED by any data in the post; the post itself says individual swings vary. No Garrett system directly; catalogued under the standing rule that technique finds count even without a tool, nearest lane the engine's player-development data world.
